text:
For most UK users, Starling is the better default choice if you want a simple, free, full-featured current account—especially if you travel or occasionally use an overdraft. Monzo is better if you value its budgeting tools, savings/investment options, and optional paid plans. Both are fully regulated UK banks with FSCS protection.
moneysavingexpert

At a glance
If you prioritise…	Better pick	Why
A free account with no subscription	Starling	Its personal account has no monthly fee and includes strong core features. 
moneysavingexpert

Budgeting and money organisation	Monzo	Pots, spending categories, bill tracking and salary sorting are Monzo’s standout strengths. 
moneysavingexpert

Travel and overseas cash	Starling	Starling charges no fees of its own for spending or withdrawing cash abroad; Monzo also has no card-spend fees but applies overseas ATM limits/charges in some cases. 
moneysavingexpert

Cheaper overdraft borrowing	Starling	Starling’s overdraft starts at 15% EAR, versus Monzo’s 19% EAR. 
moneysavingexpert

More borrowing and financial products	Monzo	Monzo offers loans, Flex credit, savings and paid plans alongside its current account. 
generationmoney.co

Human phone support	Starling	Starling is noted for 24/7 live chat and UK-based phone support. 
moneysavingexpert

Savings rate	Depends on plan	Starling’s saver is listed at 4% including a six-month bonus, while Monzo’s limited-access saver is listed at 3.45%; rates and eligibility can change. 
moneysavingexpert
Why Starling edges it

Starling is the cleaner choice if you want one main account without paying a monthly fee. It combines no-fee overseas spending and withdrawals, lower starting overdraft pricing, and straightforward budgeting features such as Spaces and virtual cards.
moneysavingexpert

It is particularly compelling if you:

Travel outside the UK or use foreign ATMs regularly.

Want to avoid subscription tiers.

May need an overdraft.

Prefer being able to call support.
moneysavingexpert

When Monzo wins

Monzo is the stronger choice if you enjoy actively managing money in the app. Its Pots, salary sorter, spending breakdowns and savings tools make it especially good for budgeting, while its paid plans add extras such as travel insurance and lifestyle perks.
moneysavingexpert

Choose Monzo if you:

Want the most polished budgeting experience.

Are likely to use savings, investments, loans or Flex.

Want optional insurance/perks and are comfortable with a paid plan.

Use it as your main account and can benefit from its account-tier features.
generationmoney.co

Practical recommendation

Open Starling if you want the best all-round free account, particularly for travel and occasional borrowing. Open Monzo instead if budgeting tools are your main priority or you want a broader in-app financial ecosystem.
moneysavingexpert

There is no need to choose only one: many people use Starling as the main spending account and Monzo for budgeting, pots and savings, or vice versa. Both offer free personal and joint accounts, so trying both is low-risk.
lilachbullock
